statement: In Chicago, the daily number of shooting incidents with a gunshot injury rises with the day's maximum temperature at Midway Airport by about the same proportion as in New York (IRR 1.146 per 5 C, 1.130 to 1.163), under the same model, so that the New York result transfers.

graph_evidence.summary: Two case-crossover studies. Rahman et al. 2023 (California 2014-2019): homicide odds +4.9% (1.6 to 8.1) per 5 C Tmax lag 0. Xu et al. 2020 (9 US cities 2007-2017): intentional homicide +9.5% (4.3 to 15.0) per 5 C mean temperature in Chicago and +8.8% (1.5 to 16.6) in New York, lag 0-7. The graph stores Xu's estimates as odds ratios 0.095 and 0.088 and Rahman's as odds ratios 4.9 and 6.2; the abstracts give percent changes, so the graph values are mis-extracted (true ORs about 1.095, 1.088, 1.049, 1.062).

Girma et al. 2023, New York City ED visits 2005-2011 (SPARCS), warm season: intentional injury among 20-25 year olds OR 1.54 (1.28 to 1.85) for daily minimum 77 F vs 48 F, lag 0-5. The only NYC violence-temperature finding in the graph.

The gun violence concept has no relationship with temperature, air temperature, heat wave, hot or extreme heat. Violence (2qLKgaxkm_), crime, aggression and violent crime have none either. The graph's heat-violence evidence is homicide and injury only.
Self-directed violence rises with temperature in 8 studies (e.g. RR 1.35, 1.26 to 1.45, PMID 35394808; per 1 C IRR 1.008, PMID 34034696). Context for the violence claim.

graph_evidence_note: Copied from heat-shootings. The graph holds no temperature-gun violence finding; its Chicago evidence is Xu et al. 2020 (homicide, +9.5% per 5 C mean temperature, 4.3 to 15.0). Descriptive, run after the city test and not part of the verdict. For temperature concepts paired with violence-side concepts (homicide, assault, aggression, violent crime, suicide, injury, gun violence) and for telework or commuting variables, list every study behind the relationships (sysgraph.relationship_studies, sysgraph.study) and tabulate the population field by country and by setting. Predicted before the lookup: fewer than 25% of studies with a readable population name a US city or a US metropolitan area, fewer than 5 studies name Chicago or New York, and the telework and commuting findings are dominated by non-US samples (UK, Netherlands, China, Australia). The graph's population field is free text and sparse, so the share with a readable population is reported with the shares.

literature.citation: Reeping PM, Hemenway D. The association between weather and the number of daily shootings in Chicago (2012-2016). Inj Epidemiol 2020;7:31.
literature.finding: Negative binomial GEE with month and year fixed effects: +34.0% (28.1 to 40.2) shootings per 10 C daily high on weekdays, +41.6% (34.7 to 48.9) on weekends and holidays; per 5 C that is IRR 1.158 and 1.190.

literature.citation: Lyons VH, Gause EL, Spangler KR, Wellenius GA, Jay J. Analysis of daily ambient temperature and firearm violence in 100 US cities. JAMA Netw Open 2022;5(12):e2247207.
literature.finding: Gun Violence Archive 2015-2020, distributed-lag models, lag 0 best: RR 1.17 (1.12 to 1.21) at the 84th percentile of Tmax vs the city median; 6.85% of shootings attributable to days above the median; Northeast attributable fraction 9.54%.

literature.citation: Xu R, Xiong X, Abramson MJ, Li S, Guo Y. Ambient temperature and intentional homicide: a multi-city case-crossover study in the US. Environ Int 2020;143:105992.
literature.finding: New York 2007-2017: +8.8% (1.5 to 16.6) intentional homicide per 5 C daily mean temperature, lag 0-7; 7.1% attributable to temperatures above the median.

prediction.magnitude: Chicago IRR per 5 C of Midway TMAX (lag 0) between 1.10 and 1.20, point estimate near 1.14.
prediction.transfers_band: The result transfers if the Chicago point estimate lies within 25% of New York's excess over 1, that is between 1.110 and 1.183 (0.146 x 0.75 and x 1.25), and the lower 95% limit exceeds 1.00.
prediction.support_if: Chicago primary IRR per 5 C in [1.110, 1.183] and its lower 95% limit above 1.00 (verdict confirmed = transfers).
prediction.refute_if: Chicago primary IRR per 5 C below 1.073 or above 1.219 (outside 50% of New York's excess), or its lower 95% limit at or below 1.00 (verdict contested = does not transfer).
prediction.otherwise: A point estimate in [1.073, 1.110) or (1.183, 1.219], with lower limit above 1.00, gives unsettled (partial transfer).
prediction.reeping_comparison: Reported without a verdict: Chicago IRR per 5 C against Reeping and Hemenway's 1.158 (weekdays) and 1.190 (weekends and holidays) from the exploratory split, and the primary model restricted to 2012-2016.

datasets.gumc-mgzr: Violence Reduction - Victims of Homicides and Non-Fatal Shootings (data.cityofchicago.org)

plan.access: concord/socrata.py with concord.socrata.DOMAIN = https://data.cityofchicago.org set in the script; the source records say kind nyc-open-data and carry the Chicago url.
plan.outcome_unit: Daily count of distinct case_number among rows of gumc-mgzr with gunshot_injury_i in ('Y','YES'), by date (date_trunc_ymd). A case can have several victims; New York's unit is the distinct incident_key, so the case is the analogous unit. Non-fatal shootings begin in 2010 in this dataset, so the period is 2010-01-01 to 2026-08-31 (the end date used for New York), with days without rows counted as zero.
plan.weather: GHCN-Daily USW00014819 (Chicago Midway), TMAX and PRCP, via concord/noaa.py. Midway is nearer the south and west sides, where most shootings occur, than O'Hare. If Midway TMAX is missing on more than 5% of days in the period, O'Hare (USW00094846) becomes primary and the registration's primary reading is taken to be that file.
plan.model: The same as heat-shootings: negative binomial GLM, log link, dispersion by maximum likelihood, robust HC0 standard errors; n ~ TMAX/5 + C(day of week) + C(month) + C(year) + holiday + (PRCP >= 1 mm). Holidays are the federal holidays plus 1 January, 4 July and 31 December (analyses.heat.common.holidays). IRR per 5 C with a 95% interval.
sensitivity: S5 O'Hare TMAX in place of Midway
S6 the 2012-2016 window of Reeping and Hemenway
S7 homicide victims only (victimization_primary = 'HOMICIDE'), distinct case_number
S8 Crimes (ijzp-q8t2): daily count of primary_type = 'HOMICIDE' plus primary_type = 'BATTERY' with description containing 'AGGRAVATED' and 'HANDGUN' or 'FIREARM'
S9 exploratory, not decisive: temperature interacted with a weekend-or-holiday indicator, for comparison with Reeping and Hemenway
plan.figure: figures/graph/transfer_chicago.png: NYC and Chicago side by side for both results.

alternatives: Different seasonal structure: Chicago's colder winters and larger seasonal range change how much of the temperature signal month terms absorb.
Different reporting: gunshot victimization is recorded by victim in the Chicago dataset; case-level counting merges victims of one event.
Different policing and gang-conflict dynamics, and the 2016 Chicago shooting spike, which year terms absorb only in level.
Temperature measured at an airport 13 km from the Loop, with a lake-breeze gradient that Central Park does not have in the same degree.
Time outdoors as the mechanism; the design cannot separate it from physiology in either city.
prior_note: The Chicago literature (Reeping and Hemenway, 1.158 and 1.190) lies inside the band, but their models differ and the band is narrow.
seen_before_registration: No value from the Chicago portal (data.cityofchicago.org) had been queried by this project: data/cache/socrata holds no Chicago file and no script in analyses/ names a Chicago dataset. Before registering, this agent read (1) the catalog search results (dataset id, name, update time) for the four datasets named below, (2) the column lists and descriptions of gumc-mgzr, 5neh-572f, 8pix-ypme and ijzp-q8t2, and (3) for the CTA stops table 8pix-ypme the station names and coordinates of the 144 stations (used to fix the Loop rule; no ridership value). No row count, date range, shooting count, ridership value or temperature value for Chicago was read, and the Midway and O'Hare weather files were not opened. The NYC side was already known: the NYC estimates in the prediction are the project's own outcomes (heat-shootings, transit-weekday-pattern). For the weekday claim the agent also recomputed, from cached NYC queries only, the NYC Delta for the rest of the subway system (all complexes outside the CBD): 4.2 points (2.2 to 6.6), recent Monday/Friday deficit 7.3%, 2019 deficit 3.1%. The registrant knows from general reading that Chicago shootings peak in summer, that Chicago downtown office occupancy has recovered less than New York's, and the abstract of Reeping and Hemenway (2020).
